# Opening: Christ had no biological father

**Definition.** By "biological father" I mean a man whose seed brought about the child's conception. I defend the standard reading: Jesus Christ was conceived in Mary without any man, by the Holy Ghost. Joseph was his supposed father and legal guardian, not his begetter.

## 1. Mary was a virgin who had not come together with any man

- [L1] Luke 1:27: "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name was Mary."
- [L1] Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- [L2] The Greek behind "came together" is *sunerchomai* (G4905, to come together, here the union of husband and wife). The conception is placed before that union. The Greek behind "virgin" is *parthenos* (G3933, a maiden who has not known a man).
- [L1] Luke 1:34: "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
- [L2] *Ginosko* (G1097, to know) is used here for sexual knowledge. *Aner* (G435, a man, a male person) shows that Mary points to the absence of any male.
- [L3] Isaiah 7:14: "Behold, a virgin shall conceive, and bear a son, and shall call his name Immanuel." The Hebrew is *almah* (H5959), which the KJV renders "virgin". Matthew 1:23 quotes it: "Behold, a virgin shall be with child, and shall bring forth a son."
- [L4] Mary says she knows no man, and the text places her pregnancy before any coming together with Joseph. Her pregnancy therefore has no male source.

## 2. The stated source of the conception is the Holy Ghost

- [L1] Matthew 1:20: "that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost."
- [L2] The preposition is *ek* (G1537, out of, from, denoting origin or source). The participle is *gennao* (G1080, to beget or conceive), in the passive. The thing begotten in her has its origin *out of* the Holy Ghost.
- [L1] Luke 1:35: "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- [L2] *Episkiazo* (G1982, to overshadow) is the word for the working of divine power. *Dia touto* ("therefore", G1223 with G3778) makes the title follow from the manner of conception.
- [L4] Luke 1:34 asks how this can be without a man. Luke 1:35 answers with the Holy Ghost and the power of the Highest, and names no man. The source of the child is stated and it is not a man.

## 3. Joseph's place is legal and supposed, not generative

- [L1] Luke 3:23: "being (as was supposed) the son of Joseph."
- [L2] *Enomizeto* (G3543, was supposed, was reckoned by custom or opinion) marks "son of Joseph" as the common opinion and not the fact.
- [L1] Matthew 1:16: "Jacob begat Joseph the husband of Mary, of whom was born Jesus, who is called Christ."
- [L2] The chain of "begat" ends at Joseph. The birth is "of whom" (*ex hes*, G1537 with a feminine singular relative), which refers to Mary alone and not to Joseph.
- [L1] Matthew 1:19: "Then Joseph her husband, being a just man, and not willing to make her a publick example, was minded to put her away privily."
- [L1] Matthew 1:20: "fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife."
- [L1] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son."
- [L2] *Ginosko* (G1097, to know) is again the idiom of marital union. It is negated up to the birth.
- [L4] Joseph is minded to put away a wife found with child, and the angel must tell him to take her. He is told the source (Matthew 1:20) and does not know it by himself. Matthew 1:25 says he had no union with her until the birth. Joseph therefore stands as husband and guardian, not as begetter.

## 4. The pattern of Scripture agrees

- [L1] Galatians 4:4: "God sent forth his son, made of a woman, made under the law."
- [L2] *Ginomai* (G1096, to become, to be made) is used of the child, with the woman named as the one he came of. No man is named in the generation.
- [L3] Genesis 3:15: "between thy seed and her seed." The Hebrew *zera* (H2233, seed) is credited to the woman.
- [L3] Jeremiah 31:22: "the LORD hath created a new thing in the earth, A woman shall compass a man." The Hebrew *bara* (H1254, to create) marks the thing as a new work of the LORD and not an ordinary generation.
- [L3] Hebrews 10:5: "a body hast thou prepared me."
- [L1] Luke 2:48: "Behold, thy father and I have sought thee sorrowing."
- [L1] Luke 2:49: "wist ye not that I must be about my father's business?"
- [L4] When Mary says "thy father" of Joseph, the child answers by pointing to "my father's business" (Luke 2:49), which is not Joseph's. The child corrects the phrase used for Joseph.

## 5. Anticipated objections

- [L1] John 6:42: "Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know?" The speakers are the crowd, "they said". [L3] Luke 3:23, "as was supposed", shows that this was common opinion.
- [L1] Luke 2:48 "thy father" is a form of address within the household. [L3] The reply at Luke 2:49 names another father.
- [L1] Romans 1:3: "made of the seed of David according to the flesh." [L2] *Sperma* (G4690, seed) is here descent, a line. [L3] Matthew 1:16 has the birth "of whom", Mary. [L3] Luke 1:32 gives the throne of "his father David", which is the line of descent and not a claim of a begetting by Joseph.

DECLARED CHAIN

1. Mary was a virgin, had not come together with Joseph, and knew no man: [L1] Luke 1:27, Matthew 1:18, Luke 1:34; [L2] *sunerchomai* (to come together), *ginosko* (to know); [L3] Isaiah 7:14 with Matthew 1:23, *almah* (virgin).
2. The conception is stated to be of the Holy Ghost: [L1] Matthew 1:20, Luke 1:35; [L2] *ek* (out of, source) and *episkiazo* (to overshadow); [L3] Luke 1:34 asks how without a man, and Luke 1:35 answers with divine power.
3. Joseph is the supposed father and husband, not the begetter: [L1] Luke 3:23, Matthew 1:16, Matthew 1:25; [L2] *enomizeto* (was supposed), *ex hes* (feminine "of whom"); [L3] Matthew 1:19-20 on Joseph's decision to put her away and the angel's explanation.
4. The wider Scripture pattern puts the woman and the new creation at the source: [L1] Galatians 4:4; [L2] *ginomai* (to be made), *bara* (to create); [L3] Genesis 3:15, Jeremiah 31:22, Hebrews 10:5, Luke 2:48-49.
5. Christ had no biological father: no man's seed was the source of his conception; the Holy Ghost is stated as the source, and the child was born of Mary.

## The question: how is it evident (Hebrews 7:14) that our Lord sprang out of Juda?

- [L1] Hebrews 7:14: "For [it is] evident that our Lord sprang out of Juda."
- [L2] *prodēlos* (G4271, plain before all men) is the word for "evident". *anatetalken* (G393 *anatellō*, to arise, spring up) is the verb for "sprang". It is the verb of a rising, and it is not *gennaō* (G1080, to beget).
- [L1] Luke 2:4-5: Joseph went up to Bethlehem "because he was of the house and lineage of David", "To be taxed with Mary his espoused wife".
- [L3] Matthew 1:20-21 and 1:24-25: Joseph is told "take unto thee Mary thy wife", he "took unto him his wife", and "he called his name JESUS".
- [L3] Numbers 1:18: "they declared their pedigrees after their families, by the house of their fathers."
- [L4] The evidence is the public register. The law enrolled by the house of the father (Numbers 1:18). Joseph, of David's house (Luke 2:4), took the mother and named the child (Matthew 1:24-25). The child was therefore enrolled in Joseph's house, and "supposed" (Luke 3:23) is the word for that reckoning. The register records the house and does not report who begat. This route is evident to all (G4271) and requires no seed from Joseph.
- [L3] Ezra 2:61 shows a man "called after their name" by a house he entered through a wife, which is a naming by house and not a begetting. Ezra 2:62 names the failure: "they were not found". The failure is a register not found (*matsa'*, H4672, to find), not a rule excluding a wife's line.
- [L3] Luke 1:42, to Mary: "blessed is the fruit of thy womb." The word *karpos* (G2590, fruit) is the word of Acts 2:30, "the fruit of his loins". The promise-word "fruit" is used of Mary's womb in Luke's own text.

## D1: virgin, no relations before the conception

ANSWER: Luke 1:27 -- D1 -- "To a virgin espoused to a man whose name was Joseph, of the house of David; and the virgin's name [was] Mary."
- [L1] The challenger grants the verse: at the angel's word she is a virgin.

- [L4] D1 says only that she was a virgin who had known no man up to the conception. Luke 1:27 and 1:34 state this, and the challenger grants both. The dispute is therefore about D2, the source of the conception.

ANSWER: Luke 1:34 -- D1 -- "Then said Mary unto the angel, How shall this be, seeing I know not a man?"
- [L1] The challenger reads "I know not" as present and the conception as future (Luke 1:31, "thou shalt conceive in thy womb"). I grant the tense.
- [L4] Her "How shall this be" asks the means, and her ground is that she knows no man. Luke 1:35 answers with "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee" [L1]. The means named is the Holy Ghost, not the espoused man.
- [L3] Luke 1:31, "thou shalt conceive in thy womb", is what the answer explains. The answer to "How" names the Holy Ghost's coming and the power's overshadowing, so a knowing by Joseph is not the means the angel gives.

ANSWER: Matthew 1:18 -- D1 -- "Now the birth of Jesus Christ was on this wise: When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
- [L1] The verse puts the finding before "they came together". The finding itself is "of the Holy Ghost".
- [L3] 1 Corinthians 7:5, "come together again, that Satan tempt you not for your incontinency", uses "come together" of marital relations.
- [L3] Luke 2:5 calls her "his espoused wife, being great with child", at a time after the taking of Matthew 1:24. So "espoused" does not mark only the time before the taking, and the challenger's equation of "came together" with the taking does not hold.
- [L4] The verse's own words date the finding before any union and name its source as the Holy Ghost. This stands as D1.

ANSWER: Deuteronomy 22:24 -- D1 -- "the man, because he hath humbled his neighbour's wife: so thou shalt put away evil from among you."
- [L1] The verse calls the betrothed "his neighbour's wife".
- [L3] Deuteronomy 22:23: "If a damsel [that is] a virgin be betrothed unto an husband, and a man find her in the city, and lie with her". The law treats lying with a betrothed virgin as an offence to be put away.

## D2: the conception was from the Holy Ghost, not from a man

ANSWER: Luke 1:35 -- D2 -- "The Holy Ghost shall come upon thee, and the power of the Highest shall overshadow thee: therefore also that holy thing which shall be born of thee shall be called the Son of God."
- [L1] The challenger reads "therefore" as pointing back to verse 32 and the coming as an anointing.

ANSWER: Luke 1:32 -- D2 -- "He shall be great, and shall be called the Son of the Highest: and the Lord God shall give unto him the throne of his father David:"

ANSWER: Matthew 1:20 -- D2 -- "But while he thought on these things, behold, the angel of the Lord appeared unto him in a dream, saying, Joseph, thou son of David, fear not to take unto thee Mary thy wife: for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost. [conceived: Gr. begotten]"

## Summary

Each of D1 to D6 stands on the footing already exhibited. The challenger's six supported links:
- Grant that she was a virgin at the angel's word (D1).
- Read the coming of Luke 1:35 from verses about the already-born (D2).
- Date a knowing before the taking by a reading of "came together" that 1 Corinthians 7:5 and Luke 2:5 do not support (D3).
- Rest the "begat" chain on a verb the text turns to the feminine "of whom was born" (D4).
- Treat Joseph's conduct as consistent with fatherhood, against a verse in which the angel's reason is the Holy Ghost as source (D3).
- Take the sign of Isaiah 7:14 as spent in Isaiah's day, against the evangelist's own application (D6).

On the verses of the KJV: the child was conceived of the Holy Ghost, born of Mary, and had no biological father.

# Opening: Christ had no human biological father

[L1] Matthew 1:18: "When as his mother Mary was espoused to Joseph, before they came together, she was found with child of the Holy Ghost."
[L2] The Greek is *ἐν γαστρὶ ἔχουσα* (*en gastri echousa*, "having in womb", with child) *ἐκ πνεύματος ἁγίου* (*ek pneumatos hagiou*, "out of Spirit holy"). The preposition *ek* (out of) names the source, and the source named is the Holy Ghost.
[L3] Matthew 1:20: "for that which is conceived in her is of the Holy Ghost." The verb is *γεννηθέν* (*gennēthen*, begotten or conceived), and it is again followed by *ek pneumatos hagiou*.

[L1] Matthew 1:18 says she was found with child "before they came together".

[L3] Matthew 1:25: "And knew her not till she had brought forth her firstborn son." The verb *ἐγίνωσκεν* (*eginōsken*, was knowing) is the verb for marital knowledge, and it is negated up to the birth. [L3] Matthew 1:19: "Joseph her husband, being a just man... was minded to put her away privily." [L4] A just man would not plan to put her away if he were the cause of the pregnancy. ## Final words

Line upon line, the record reads the subject this way. The promised seed is David's, "of the fruit of his loins, according to the flesh" (Acts 2:30). It is plain by the father's house (Hebrews 7:14; Numbers 1:2), and that house is Joseph's (Luke 2:4). The father is named by Mary, "thy father and I" (Luke 2:48), by the town (John 6:42) and by a disciple (John 1:45). "Of the Holy Ghost" stands in the same row as "Joseph, thou son of David" and "Mary thy wife" (Matthew 1:20). [L4] Footed on Acts 2:30 and Luke 2:48 with Genesis 4:1: Christ had a biological father, Joseph, the husband of Mary, of the house and lineage of David.
